claim: In the 2022 presidential runoff (a genuine presidential-type second round, not legislative), 42% of Mélenchon's first-round electorate transferred to Macron and 17% to Le Pen, with 41% not expressing a vote (24% abstention + 17% blank/null) — down from a roughly two-thirds barrage rate for the equivalent electorate in 2017.
stance_target: vote-transfer/barrage coefficients are stable across election type (legislative vs presidential) or robust to being applied unchanged across a five-year span
scope_conditions: France, presidential second round, Mélenchon 2022 first-round electorate, compared to 2017
quoted_support: Un tiers (42%) des électeurs de Jean-Luc Mélenchon a choisi Emmanuel Macron pour 17% Marine Le Pen [...] avec 41% des électeurs de Jean-Luc Mélenchon qui ne s'est pas exprimé cette année (24% d'abstention, 17% de vote blancs ou nuls), pour un tiers en 2017 (17% d'abstention, 15% de vote blanc et nul).

claim: The 2022 presidential runoff barrage/report-de-voix rate for the LR (Pécresse) electorate toward Macron was 53%, versus 18% to Le Pen, notably lower than the ~97% legislative NFP-to-Ensemble transfer rate cited for 2024 duels, showing barrage strength differs by election type even in the same direction.
stance_target: the 2024 legislative front-républicain transfer matrix (e.g. 97% NFP-to-Ensemble in Ensemble/RN duels) is a reliable proxy for presidential-runoff-type transfer behavior
scope_conditions: France, presidential second round 2022, centre-right (LR/Pécresse) electorate
quoted_support: plus de la moitié (53%) des électeurs de Valérie Pécresse ont aussi fait le choix du Président sortant, pour 18% Marine Le Pen.

claim: Own-camp retention was highly asymmetric in the 2022 runoff: 98% of Macron's first-round voters reiterated their vote for him versus 91% of Le Pen's own first-round voters reiterating for her, meaning even 'core' vote retention (not cross-bloc transfer) varies and is not simply 100% by assumption.
stance_target: modeling assumptions used in transfer-matrix-based projections
quoted_support: une meilleure mobilisation de l'électorat premier tour d'Emmanuel Macron (98% ont réitéré leur choix pour 91% dans l'électorat de Marine Le Pen)

claim: Between 2017 and 2022, Marine Le Pen's presidential-runoff vote share rose 11 points among workers (to 67%), 11 points among employees (to 57%), 8 points among intermediate professions, and 5 points among executives, indicating multi-year secular erosion of anti-RN transfer patterns predates the 2024-2025 window entirely.
stance_target: erosion of anti-RN transfer coefficients is a longer-run secular trend, not a sudden 2024-2025 phenomenon
scope_conditions: France, presidential runoffs 2017 vs 2022, by socio-professional category
quoted_support: L'assise de Marine Le Pen s'est quand même bien élargie par rapport à 2017, avec 11 points gagnés chez les ouvriers (elle était à 56% en 2017), 11 points chez les employés (46% en 2017), 8 points au sein des professions intermédiaires (33%), 5 points chez les cadres (18% en 2017).
